unperturbed

un-per-TURBD · adjective

What It Means

Unperturbed is not perturbed or agitated; calm, especially in the face of something that would normally cause distress.

The pilot's unperturbed voice over the intercom, calmly describing the turbulence as 'a little bumpy,' kept the whole cabin from panicking.

Example

Reporters hurled hostile questions at the CEO for nearly an hour, but she remained entirely unperturbed, answering each one in the same calm, measured voice she'd used at the start.

Unperturbed means undisturbed and calm despite something that would normally cause distress -- the hostile questions don't shake the CEO's composure at all.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

unruffled: Unruffled means showing no sign of disturbance because none was felt -- the surface stays smooth since nothing underneath is churning. Unperturbed is its close twin: both describe calm that is real all the way down, not calm that is performed while feelings churn inside.

composed: Composed means keeping your feelings under control so they don't show -- steady voice, settled face -- even while you are churning inside. Unperturbed is different: it means you are genuinely not disturbed at all, calm in the face of something that would rattle most people.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

flustered: agitated and confused

agitated: troubled or nervous

Where it sits · how steady under real pressure — relaxed → unperturbed → unflappable

relaxed vs. unperturbed: Relaxed is milder than unperturbed -- relaxed is ordinary ease when nothing is pressing on you, while unperturbed means staying calm while something genuinely alarming is happening.

unflappable vs. unperturbed: Unflappable describes someone who is never rattled, no matter what happens -- an even steadier, more absolute version of unperturbed.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — un-

prefix — un-: not (Old English)

root — perturb

root — perturb: to disturb greatly (Latin perturbare)

Put it together

Put it together: Unperturbed comes from un- ('not') + perturb ('to disturb greatly,' from Latin per- 'thoroughly' + turbare 'to throw into confusion') -- literally 'not thoroughly disturbed.'

Use the root in a new word: turbulence

Use the root in a new word: turbulence: The plane shook through ten minutes of turbulence before the ride smoothed out.

Root Check

Word Choice

Unperturbed describes staying calm specifically in the face of something that would normally cause distress or agitation -- a crisis, a hostile question, bad news. That's different from nonchalant, which describes a more general attitude of not caring or not being bothered, even without any particular provocation. Someone can be unperturbed by a real emergency but nonchalant about something that simply doesn't interest them.
